title: Principles of Eventual Consistency
byline: Sebastian Burckhardt · Foundations and Trends in Programming Languages, 2014
note: The Drive file is named “Linerarity of Consistency”; the book is Burckhardt’s monograph. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A formal framework for specifying and verifying replicated systems that stay available by letting replicas diverge temporarily. Burckhardt models what clients observe as histories, explains them with abstract executions (visibility and arbitration orders over events), and states consistency guarantees as axioms on those orders. Replicated data types such as counters, registers and sets get precise specifications, and the guarantees are arranged in a hierarchy from basic eventual consistency through causal consistency to sequential consistency and linearizability. The second half gives a pseudocode language and its operational semantics, protocol templates (epidemic, broadcast, global-sequence), a version of the CAP theorem, and correctness proofs connecting implementations to specifications.
